newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn won't confirm report it eyes 2-point VAT hike.
newsitem.headline: Bonn won't confirm report it eyes 2-point VAT hike.

text.p: The German finance ministry on Saturday declined to confirm a newspaper report that Bonn will raise value-added-tax (VAT) by two percentage points to 17 percent from January 1, 1999 as part of a broad tax reform.
A spokeswoman for the finance ministry contacted by Reuters said she could not confirm that a decision had been reached to raise VAT by two percentage points.
She said the ruling coalition was scheduled to hold further talks on its tax reform plans next week.

The report in the Bild am Sonntag newspaper said Finance Minister Theo Waigel had confirmed that VAT would be raised and quoted him as saying the reduced VAT rate on products like food, newspapers and books would remain unchanged at seven percent.
But the plan for a two-percentage point hike mentioned in the report was unsourced.

Bonn is widely expected to raise VAT to help finance a tax reform with which Waigel aims to lighten the burden on German taxpayers by a net 30 billion marks to help boost jobs and investment in the country's cost-laden economy.
In a copy of an article made available ahead of publication on Sunday, Bild am Sonntag quoted Waigel as saying: "With a value-added-tax rise we will maintain the reduced VAT rate at seven percent."
"That means the impact for low earners, pensioners or large families will be very acceptable socially."
A tax policy working group chaired by Waigel is due to complete its work next week.
